geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a subtle bend to reduce the blocky rigidity while preserving the main mass as one readable bar.
A modest bend strengthens the spatial rule and helps the mass read as one continuous gesture.
Use enough subdivisions to keep the bend smooth and executable in section.
Retain the current frontage-parallel direction so the court still opens coherently to access.
Deepen the void to create a more legible public court and a stronger ground response.
Keep the void opening aligned with the verified access side.

graph_edits.rationale: Wrap the rectilinear host into a gentler bar/wing logic so the dominant gesture becomes more site-responsive without losing the current U-shaped court.
Keep the mass compact but extend it slightly along the frontage axis to strengthen hierarchy and ground the public void.
Deepen the court/undercut so the open space reads as usable public threshold rather than a shallow notch.
Preserve the access-aligned opening to keep the street-facing edge legible and programmatically aligned.

rationale: The candidate is legible in plan and overall as an open U-shaped bar with a clear void, and it does respond to the verified access edge with a visible open side. However, the mass is still quite box-like and the section reads weakly: the upper carve is shallow, the silhouette is repetitive, and the form does not yet convincingly support the neighborhood-living brief with an active ground threshold and a more meaningful public interior. It is coherent across views, but not strongly enough in section or program relationship to pass as-is.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and sculptural than this candidate; do not copy the curved roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central void and bridge-like upper connection can support a neighborhood/public threshold program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; tower/podium composition is not transferable here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation around a courtyard can create public space while preserving a clear hierarchy of volumes.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is less resolved in section and reads more as a hollowed block than an active street building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple rectilinear mass with a large carved void and upper overhang gives a legible public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference leans flatter and more horizontal; candidate is more boxed and less site-responsive.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated massing with a central void and subtle roof/profile variation can keep the building grounded and public.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the sectional richness and winged continuity seen in the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard organization with connected wings supports neighborhood living and a clear public interior figure.

warnings: Parcel containment could not be independently verified from the supplied view raster, so no deterministic pass is assumed.
The open void is legible, but its publicness is moderate rather than robust; it risks reading as a simple subtraction rather than a usable social court.
